name: pollux-ui
description: Use Pollux templates and layouts through safe, verified generator workflows.

interface.shortDescription: Safe, verified Pollux generator and layout workflows.
interface.longDescription: Inspect, scaffold, apply layouts, generate CRUD surfaces, and verify Pollux projects through canonical repository workflows.
defaultPrompt: Inspect this repository and identify the applicable Pollux workflow.
Create a Pollux workspace from a registered skeleton.
Verify Pollux package, generator, and target drift.

pollux-inspect.shortDescription: Inspect Pollux surfaces, targets, and support status.
pollux-inspect.defaultPrompt: Use $pollux-inspect to report which Pollux generator surface, target, and verification gates apply to this repository.

pollux-create-workspace.shortDescription: Scaffold a new app from a Pollux skeleton.
pollux-create-workspace.defaultPrompt: Use $pollux-create-workspace to scaffold a new Pollux app workspace from a registered skeleton.

pollux-apply-layout.shortDescription: Apply the Pollux admin shell to a target.
pollux-apply-layout.defaultPrompt: Use $pollux-apply-layout to apply the Pollux admin shell and design tokens to a framework target.

pollux-generate-crud.shortDescription: Regenerate Pollux CRUD pages and backends.
pollux-generate-crud.defaultPrompt: Use $pollux-generate-crud to regenerate Pollux CRUD output from json-files metadata through the canonical CLI.

pollux-verify.shortDescription: Run Pollux drift, package, and target gates.
pollux-verify.defaultPrompt: Use $pollux-verify to run the Pollux package, drift, and target verification gates for recent changes.

capabilities.description: Read-only discovery of repositories, generator surfaces, skeleton provenance, targets, support status, and required resource IDs.
preconditions: running inside a checkout that contains the ./pollux CLI
postconditions: structured proposed operation with exact affected paths

capabilities.description: Create a fresh application workspace from a registered boilerplate skeleton through staged, atomic copy with provenance.
preconditions: explicit user request naming skeleton and destination
destination is empty or does not exist

capabilities.description: Apply or port a Pollux admin shell (sidebar, topbar, tokens, content canvas) into a supported framework target.
preconditions: explicit user request with exact target
target layout resource is packaged and hash-verified
affected files classified as handwritten-host, generator-owned, or generated
postconditions: responsive shell, keyboard navigation, and target build verified

capabilities.description: Regenerate legacy TypeScript pages, standalone Go backend, or standalone framework CRUD from json-files metadata through the canonical Pollux CLI.
preconditions: explicit backend/target selection; no silent defaults
generated paths are clean or user approved --accept-generated-overwrite for named files
postconditions: canonical fmt pipeline ran (oxlint --fix, then oxfmt)
generated ownership manifest updated by the CLI only

capabilities.description: Run plugin package validation, source-drift checks, generator drift gates, and target verification matrices matched to changed resources.
preconditions: package snapshot built from the current source revision
postconditions: layered verification result separating package, host, generator, and runtime gates

skills.description: Inspect Pollux generators, templates, layouts, skeletons, and support status before generation or layout work. Use when a user asks what Pollux can generate, whether a Next.js, React Router, or Astro target is production-ready or supported, which target or template applies, or what checks are required.
Create a new application workspace from a registered Pollux skeleton (Next.js, React Router/Remix, Astro). Use when a user asks to scaffold, bootstrap, or start a new Pollux app from a skeleton.

Apply or port the Pollux admin layout — sidebar, topbar, design tokens, theme behavior, content canvas — into a supported framework target. Use when a user asks to reuse the Pollux shell, port the layout, or sync design tokens.

Generate or regenerate Pollux CRUD pages and backends from json-files entity metadata — legacy TypeScript /generated pages, the Go backend, or standalone Next.js/React Router/Astro targets. Use when entity metadata or templates change.

Verify Pollux work: plugin package conformance, resource and generator drift, target build/test gates, and release readiness. Use when a user asks to check drift, validate the plugin, or prove a Pollux change is safe.
